article_title: MCP TypeScript SDK 2.3.0 Enforces One Server Per Request, Limits Redirects to the Same Origin and Adds Opt-In Tool Input and Token Audience Checks

content_preview.title: MCP TypeScript SDK 2.3.0 Enforces One Server Per Request, Limits Redirects to the Same Origin and Adds Opt-In Tool Input and Token Audience Checks
content_preview.summary: The Model Context Protocol TypeScript SDK shipped 2.3.0 on October 2 and 1.32.0 the same day, with same-origin redirect handling by default and two off-by-default options; 2.3.1 followed on October 5.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) TypeScript SDK published version 2.3.0 on October 2, 2026, at 17:55 UTC, according to its [release page](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases/tag/v2.3.0). The release lists five upgrade notes: a one-server-per-request rule, a same-origin redirect policy, two new options that are off unless set, a change to how `prompts/get` handles missing arguments, and a raised minimum for `eventsource-parser`. editor_notes.content_quality: Compact, well-structured Briefing (640 words, within the 300-800 range). Leads with the 2.3.0 release, then per-release sections, then an explicit 'What We Don't Know' section. No orphan URLs: the three body source URLs are exactly the three in article.sources; the only other link is the internal /article/2026-09/30-... link.
editor_notes.source_verification: All three sources are first-party release notes on the project's own GitHub repository (modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk); no third-party outlets are cited. Snapshots read: source-0.html.gz (v2.3.0), source-1.html.gz (1.32.0), source-2.html.gz (v2.3.1); all HTTP 200, suspicious_patterns null for each. Because the snapshots are 200KB GitHub HTML pages, I also re-fetched the raw release bodies and timestamps via the GitHub REST API (gh api repos/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk/releases/tags/<tag>) rather than rely on a summarizing fetcher, and cross-checked against the snapshot relative-time datetime attributes; they agree. v2.3.0: published_at 2026-10-02T17:55:03Z (article: October 2, 2026, 17:55 UTC - correct). 1.32.0: published_at 2026-10-02T17:28:24Z (article: same day, 17:28 UTC - correct). v2.3.1: published_at 2026-10-05T11:54:56Z (article: October 5 - correct; the rendered page shows '05 Oct' without a year, but the snapshot datetime attribute and API give 2026, and the article states only 'October 5' without overstating a time). Per-release attribution verified: the five 2.3.0 upgrade notes (one server per request incl. #2889 cheap-server remark; same-origin redirects with redirectPolicy: 'follow' and browser failure; maxToolInputElements and expectedResource off unless set, Express upgrade with server; prompts/get validated as {}; eventsource-parser >= 3.0.8 with 100 MB ~1 min/1.7 GB to <1 s/~0.5 GB) are all in the v2.3.0 notes, as are the separate 50 MB/13 s Fixes entry, the <scheme>://* origin entries (moz-extension://*) and the SSEClientTransport single refresh after a 401. The 1.32.0 notes contain the redirect and opt-in-option upgrade notes naming StreamableHTTPClientTransport and SSEClientTransport, the in-memory task store session fix, the examples idle-session/session-map cap change, and the SECURITY.md pointer to GitHub Security Advisories - all attributed to 1.32.0 in the article. The v2.3.1 notes contain the server-legacy requireBearerAuth expectedResource change (#2952), correctly attributed to 2.3.1 and described as the option 'server 2.3.0 added'. The article does not claim 2.3.1 added it to the main server package.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, date, option name and package name traces to the cited release notes. Security framing is restrained: the article does not use words like vulnerability, flaw or severity, does not infer CVEs, and the 'What We Don't Know' section correctly states the notes cite no CVE or advisory (verified: no CVE-/GHSA- strings in any of the three pages; the only security mention is the SECURITY.md docs change in 1.32.0). The statement that servers not setting the new options 'keep their previous behavior on tool input size and token audience' is a direct consequence of 'off unless you set them' and is acceptable. The 'does not state how many deployments rely on...' remark is an accurate statement of absence. The token-audience gloss is taken verbatim from the notes.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, descriptive, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. The title uses 'Enforces' for the one-server-per-request rule, which mirrors the notes' 'now rejects while the instance is already connected'.
editor_notes.originality: No prior coverage of the MCP TypeScript SDK 2.3.0 release in src/content/articles. The linked 2026-09/30 Python SDK OAuth article exists at that exact slug, uses the correct singular /article/<YYYY-MM>/<slug> form, and is explicitly described as a separate project, so no conflation. Writer skipped the research log; I ran the checks myself (word count 640, link and orphan-URL diff clean).
concerns: The summary and several bullets compress the redirect rule; the notes also allow http to https on the same host, which the article does include. No concerns requiring correction.
The 2.3.0 'five upgrade notes' count matches the five bullets under 'Upgrade notes' in the release body.
recommendations: For future release briefings, include the research log with the submission and state publication year for dates shown without a year on the release page.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully attributed Briefing based entirely on first-party release notes. Dates, per-release attribution and security language all check out against raw API text. APPROVE.
